name: Scavenging Deathknell
summary: In Deathknell, newly awakened Forsaken gather supplies for the recruits rising from nearby graves. Deathguard Saltain sends them to search the blighted settlement for abandoned boxes and crates, where the Forsaken must find what they need to survive.

sections.title: A Pragmatic Resurrection
sections.body: Newly raised Forsaken wake in Deathknell with little to call their own. Deathguard Saltain sends them to gather what the recruits still climbing from their graves need: clothing and arms. The Forsaken must salvage supplies to outfit those newly risen, with every usable piece put to work.

sections.title: Scraping by in Tirisfal
sections.body: Deathknell holds remnants of its former human inhabitants and supplies abandoned during the kingdom’s fall to the Scourge. Deathguards send newly awakened Forsaken to recover usable goods from boxes and crates scattered through the town. The Forsaken expect no charity from the living and must depend on their own effort to survive.

faq.q: Why does Deathguard Saltain need scavenged goods?
faq.answer: Deathguard Saltain gathers equipment for newly awakened Forsaken rising in the nearby cemetery. Scavenged clothing, boots, and tools help keep fresh recruits from wandering the blighted hills unarmed and defenseless.

faq.q: Where are the scavenged goods found?
faq.answer: The goods lie in stacks of boxes and crates throughout Deathknell, near abandoned buildings and quiet corners of the settlement.
Saltain is a Deathguard stationed in Deathknell who evaluates fresh undead recruits and puts them to work. He enforces order and survival through harsh discipline.

faq.q: Why don't the Forsaken have standard military supplies here?
faq.answer: The Forsaken are a young, beleaguered people facing hostile living enemies and mind-controlled Scourge. With resources stretched thin in Deathknell, they reclaim and reuse what was left in the ruins.

faq.q: What happens after completing this task?
faq.answer: Saltain gives the recruit a piece of salvaged armor from the communal stockpile. It marks the recruit’s passage from an unproven corpse to a functional soldier of the Dark Lady.

faq.q: Why are so many new undead rising in Deathknell right now?
faq.answer: As the Lich King’s grip on his servants weakens, some of Lordaeron’s dead break free with their minds intact. Confused, they rise from their graves and need immediate guidance.

angles.text: As an undead, you learn the hard terms of your new life: no one in Azeroth offers pity or charity, so the Forsaken must salvage their future from the dirt.
The Forsaken are allied with the Horde across the sea, yet outposts like Deathknell must meet daily needs through desperate local scavenging rather than foreign aid.
